GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The spec treats user and developer messages interchangeably, except that when both are present in a conversation, the developer messages have greater authority; when user/developer conflicts are not relevant and there is no risk of confusion, the word "user" will sometimes be used as shorthand for "user or developer".

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - user_definition: A user of a product made by OpenAI or a third-party application built on the OpenAI API.
  - developer_definition: A customer of the OpenAI API who may add intelligence to software applications or create natural language interfaces consumed by end users.
  - authority_levels_hierarchy: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1_170_n091' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):

When user/developer conflicts are not relevant and there is no risk of confusion, the word "user" will sometimes be used as shorthand for "user or developer".
